title: Type Conversion
definition: Type conversion transforms a value from one representation or type domain to another while exposing possible loss of precision or meaning.
purpose: Make boundary transformations explicit, testable, and safe.
history: Languages and interchange systems define conversion rules because external data rarely arrives in the exact runtime type a program needs.
mental_model: Conversion is a checkpoint with an input contract, transformation rule, validation result, and possible loss report.
analogy: Currency exchange changes representation under a rule; the analogy fails because programming conversions may reject input or silently discard information.
common_mistakes: Ignoring leading zeros, range, precision, or absence
industry_notes: Convert at explicit boundaries, preserve raw input when auditability matters, and reject ambiguous or out-of-range data.
ai_notes: AI-generated conversion code must be tested with normal, boundary, invalid, ambiguous, and precision-risk inputs.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to identify both precision loss and domain-meaning loss in a conversion table.
exercise_candidates: Mark safe, rejected, and lossy conversions
lab_candidates: Build and defend a conversion policy
